title: Expert explorer (/experts)
summary: The explorer is a warm heading over a grid of cards that say only a name, one free-text line and a price. A member cannot start from her need, cannot compare two experts without opening both, and sees three blank monogram panels where people should be. The change that matters most is the card: give it a face (or a compact layout when there is none), a profession and focus, languages, how and where sessions happen, the next open time and a checked-registration mark, then put areas of care above the grid as the way in.
strengths: The heading and lead are in the right voice: "Real people with real training. Pick someone whose work fits you, then meet by video, by phone or in person." Keep them.
On phones the card turns into a compact row (small portrait left, text right), so a short list fits in one screen (01-experts.mobile.jpg).

Ordering is disclosed. "How we order experts" links to the ranking terms, and the source labels the paid plan honestly ("Top Expert · paid plan", "Top Expert first (paid plan)"). Few marketplaces are this open; make it more visible rather than changing it.
The trust line has the right content: "Before a profile goes live, our team checks the expert's professional registration."
The whole card is one link and one tab stop, and the free option is said in plain words ("Free session available").
The source already has a first-run state for an empty directory with three next steps (newsletter, how Eleva works, are you an expert). The pattern is right; it only needs a design pass.

findings.title: A member cannot start from her need
findings.detail: The page opens with a heading and goes straight to people. There is no search field, no areas of care, no mode or language choice. A member arrives with a need (pelvic pain after birth, breastfeeding, anxiety in pregnancy), not with a name. In the source, area chips only appear once two areas have experts, and language and sort only appear from 12 experts, so at launch size the page offers nothing to narrow or even to explain what Eleva covers. The teal search button in the mobile header looks like search but sits in the same slot as the desktop "Find an expert" link, which on this page points back to itself.
findings.recommendation: Put areas of care above the grid from day one as photo or icon tiles with a count ("Pelvic health · 3 experts") and show areas with nobody yet as "Opening soon" rather than hiding them, so the page teaches the catalogue. Add one plain search field ("What do you need help with?") that matches areas, service names and expert names. Keep two always-on chips next to it: language and how you meet (video, phone, in person). Hide the header "Find an expert" button on this page.

findings.title: Cards carry too little to choose on
findings.detail: Each card shows a name, one free-text line and a price. It does not say what the person is (physiotherapist, midwife), what she focuses on, which languages she speaks, whether sessions are by video or in a city, when she is next free, or that her registration was checked. The source can show two areas of care as a quiet line, but only when the expert has picked categories, so a new expert's card falls back to almost nothing. To compare three experts a member has to open three profiles.
findings.recommendation: Fix a card content model with required fields: photo, name with a checked-registration mark, profession and up to two focus areas, languages, how you meet ("Video · In person in Lisboa"), next open time ("Next: Mon 16 Nov") and price from. Make profession and at least one area required before a profile can be listed, so no card depends on a free-text headline. Add a quiet "View profile" affordance; keep the whole card as one link.

findings.title: The missing-photo placeholder takes over the card
findings.detail: On desktop each card gives about 290px of its 420px to a pale gradient panel with a monogram circle (AQ, FM, PM). Three of them in a row read as an unfinished page, and the only photograph on the screen belongs to the expert-recruitment band below. New experts will often have no photo on day one, so this is the default look of the directory, not an edge case.
findings.recommendation: Ask for a portrait before a profile can be listed (a publish gate in expert setup, with guidance on a good photo). For any profile that still has none, use the compact layout at every breakpoint: a small avatar beside the text, so the card's weight goes to profession, focus and next time instead of an empty panel. Order profiles with a photo ahead of those without inside the same sort.

findings.title: Filters cover two of the things members filter on
findings.detail: The captures show no controls because the directory is under 12 experts. Read from the source, the full set is a language select, a sort select and an "Apply filters" button in a grey box. There is no filter for how you meet, location, price or availability, the native selects need a separate submit, and nothing shows how many experts will match. On a phone a form row above the list pushes the first expert down.
findings.recommendation: Use a chip row that applies on tap: area, language, how you meet, city (only when in person is chosen), price, and "Free first chat". Show applied filters as removable chips with a result count ("7 experts"). On phones open one "Filters" bottom sheet with a sticky button that carries the count ("Show 7 experts") and a "Clear all".

findings.title: Checked registration and ordering are a footnote
findings.detail: The strongest trust statement on the page, that Eleva checks each expert's professional registration before the profile goes live, is one line of small grey text under the grid, next to the "How we order experts" link. A member choosing someone for her health reads the cards first and may never reach it. Nothing on a card repeats it, and the current order (name A to Z) is not stated anywhere.
findings.recommendation: Move the statement above the grid as a short line with a check icon, and repeat it as a small mark beside each name that opens a one-sentence explanation. State the order next to the count ("3 experts · sorted A to Z") with "How we order experts" beside it. When Top Expert placement is active, label it on the card itself, as the source already does on desktop, and show the same label on phones (today the badge is hidden below the sm breakpoint).

findings.title: An expert who cannot be booked is listed like the others
findings.detail: The third card (Patricia Mota) has no price row because she has no services yet. It looks like a rendering gap, and tapping it leads to a profile that says she is not taking bookings. In a list of three, one dead end is a third of the experience.
findings.recommendation: List an expert only once one service is published. If the founder wants early profiles visible, label the card "Opening soon", sort it last, and replace the price row with "Tell me when bookings open". For bookable experts fill the same row with the next open time so every card ends on something a member can act on.

findings.title: The recruitment band outweighs the directory
findings.detail: "Bring your practice to Eleva" is a 470px dark band with the page's only photograph on desktop, and on phones it is about 690px tall, longer than the list of experts above it (about 470px). A member's page ends on a message for someone else, and the strongest visual on the screen is not an expert she can book.
findings.recommendation: End the member's page with help for the member: a short "Not sure who to choose?" block that asks what she needs and suggests an area or a free first chat, with a link to how Eleva works. Reduce the expert invitation to one quiet line with a link ("Are you a women's health professional? Bring your practice to Eleva").

findings.title: Few-results and no-results states stop short
findings.detail: With three experts the page is a heading, one row of cards and white space. Nothing says how many experts there are or that the list is growing. Read from the source, a filter that matches nobody shows "No experts match these filters yet." with a single "See all experts" button, which throws away every choice the member made instead of helping her loosen one.
findings.recommendation: Show a count and frame a short list as chosen ("3 experts, each with a checked registration"). When filters leave few or no results, keep the results visible, list the applied filters as removable chips under "See more experts", and say which one to drop. When an area has nobody yet, offer "Tell me when a [area] expert joins" and the nearest area that does have experts.

findings.title: Price and label details
findings.detail: "From €45.00" carries cents that add nothing and make the price look longer than it is. The price has no unit, so a member cannot tell whether it is for 20 or 60 minutes. The eyebrow "FIND YOUR EXPERT" repeats the heading directly under it.
findings.recommendation: Show whole euros when there are no cents ("From €45") and add the shortest session length ("From €45 · 45 min"). Replace the eyebrow with something the heading does not say, such as the count ("3 experts in Portugal and Spain"), or remove it.

findings.title: After the name every line on the card has the same weight, and the portraits do not match
findings.detail: In the 2026-11-15 capture (slice D2.2) each card has four lines in the same small grey sans under the name: the registration mark, the headline, the areas and the price. The price or "Free session available" is the last item of a dot-separated line, and on a phone it breaks in two ("Free" on one line, "session available" on the next). No fact has a fixed place, so comparing three experts means reading three whole cards. The portraits differ in crop and distance (a close face, a half-length studio shot, a street scene, a clinical uniform), which makes the grid look uneven even when everyone has a photo.
findings.recommendation: End every card with two or three fixed cells, each a small label above a value (Next time, Meets by, From), divided by thin rules, so the same fact sits in the same place on every card. Keep the areas on a line of their own and never let the price wrap. Crop every portrait to one ratio with the face in the same position, and give experts a short photo guide at the publish step (head and shoulders, plain light background, daylight).

references.pattern: Result card with everything needed to choose
references.why: Each tutor row holds a photo, name with a verified mark, "Professional" and "Super Tutor" tags, what they teach, languages spoken with level, a two-line pitch, a price with its unit ("$41, 50-min lesson"), three numbers (reviews, students, lessons) and the booking button. The headline states the count ("100+ Japanese tutors") and filters sit in one row above. A messages panel is open over the right side of this capture. Education marketplace, kept for the card structure.
references.apply: The Eleva card content model: photo, name plus checked-registration mark, profession and focus, languages, price with session length, and one action. Whole-number prices with a unit.
references.query: therapist directory search results with filters

references.pattern: Count, one Filters button, availability inside the card
references.why: The list opens with a shield icon and a count ("265 In-network providers") and a single Filters button. Each card gives photo, name with credential, specialty, rating and review count, distance and address, then tabs for in-person and video visits over a strip of days that shows how many appointments each day has.
references.apply: A count with a trust icon at the top of the list, profession directly under the name, and next availability on the card split by how you meet.
references.query: doctor appointment app search results with filters

references.pattern: Two filter chips and a bottom sheet for a short list
references.why: A European health product with a small therapist list. Two chips only (Specialty, language). The card behind the sheet shows a photo, name, "Available on Thursday", the languages spoken and specialty tags. The sheet lists specialties as checkboxes with one button, "Show therapists".
references.apply: For a directory of a few dozen experts, two or three chips are enough: area, language, how you meet. Each opens a sheet with a clear apply button. "Available on Thursday" is the tone for Eleva's next-time line.
references.query: doctor appointment app search results with filters

references.pattern: Category tiles with counts and "Coming soon"
references.why: A young catalogue shown honestly. A row of photo tiles names each category with "16 available", "5 available" or "Coming soon", and the chosen category's results sit below with price from and rating. Sparse categories still show the breadth of what is offered. Travel marketplace, kept for how it handles a small catalogue.
references.apply: Areas of care as tiles above the grid with counts, and "Opening soon" for areas and experts that are not bookable yet, so nothing looks broken and the member learns what Eleva covers.
references.query: wellness booking marketplace search results with available times

references.pattern: Applied filters as chips, check badge and match reasons on the card
references.why: A filter panel on the left with a count ("Filters (7)") and "Clear all"; every applied filter repeats as a removable chip above the results. Each caregiver card shows a "Background Checked" tag, a short quoted review, and a line of ticks for the filters this person matches ("English, 3+ stars, +4 more matches"). Price sits top right with its unit.
references.apply: Removable chips for applied filters, a checked-registration tag on every card, and a line that says why this expert matches what the member asked for.
references.query: therapist directory search results with filters

references.pattern: "Tell us what you need" prompt above compact cards
references.why: Above the directory a box asks "Tell us what you need and we'll match you with the right partner". The cards below use a small avatar beside the name rather than a large image, so a card with a weak photo still looks complete: tier tag, rating, two-line description, location, languages, service tags and a footer with price from and a Contact button. Software marketplace, kept for the structure.
references.apply: A need-led entry point for members who do not know which kind of expert they need, and the compact card layout for profiles that have no portrait.
references.query: therapist directory search results with filters

references.pattern: Mobile filter sheet with visible sort and a verified toggle
references.why: One sheet holds everything. Sort is three labelled tiles (Best match, Nearest, Top rated) so the current order is always visible, then a max price slider, an "Only show: Fresha verified" switch with a line of explanation under it, amenity chips, and a sticky footer with "Clear all" and "Apply".
references.apply: On phones, one Filters sheet with sort shown as named choices, a plain line explaining any trust filter, and a sticky apply button.
references.query: tutoring marketplace search filters bottom sheet

references.pattern: Few results: "Get more matches" with removable filters
references.why: The search returns one tutor. Under that card a block titled "Get more matches" says "Try removing some filters to see more tutors" and lists each applied filter by group (Focus on, Price, Other) as a chip with an x. The member loosens one choice instead of starting again.
references.apply: Eleva's few-results and no-results state: keep what matched, then show the applied filters as chips to remove one at a time, in place of a single "See all experts" reset.
references.query: Preply tutor profile page

references.pattern: Next bookable times on the result card
references.why: The list states a count ("21 venues nearby") beside a Filters button. Each result names the matching service with its length and price, then shows the next three times as buttons (10.00, 10.15, 10.30) and "See more", so a member can book from the list.
references.apply: Fill the last row of each Eleva card with the next open time, or two or three times, linked straight into booking, so every card ends on an action.
references.query: wellness booking marketplace search results with available times

references.pattern: A list of one that still feels complete
references.why: "Available therapists (1)" states the count without apology. The single card shows photo, name, licence type, then four icon rows (in-network, degree, specialties, language) and an appointment time button. Selecting it opens a side panel with Specialties, "Approach to care" and "More about me".
references.apply: How a very short list should look: an honest count, credential-led cards with icon rows, and a preview of the expert's approach before the member commits to opening the profile.
references.query: therapist directory search results with filters

references.pattern: Paid placement labelled on the card, sort order stated
references.why: Paid listings carry an "Ad" label in the seller line of the card itself, and the sort control at the top right names the current order ("Most relevant"). Applied filters show as chips. Retail marketplace, kept for the labelling only.
references.apply: Keep "Top Expert · paid plan" on the card at every breakpoint and state the current order beside the count, with "How we order experts" next to it.
references.query: marketplace search results with sponsored listing label and sort menu

references.pattern: Category chips and a name search over a portrait grid
references.why: "All 1-on-1 Sessions" has a search field for teachers and a wrap of category chips with "All Categories" selected. The grid is led by portraits with name, a one-line role and a price range. One teacher uses an illustration instead of a photo and the grid still holds because the tile is square and the same size. Education product, kept for the layout.
references.apply: Always-visible area chips plus a name search, and a consistent portrait tile. It also shows why a portrait-led grid needs real photos: the cards work because nearly everyone has one.
references.query: therapist directory search results with filters

references.pattern: A portrait grid where every photo shares one light, crop and backdrop
references.why: Under a one-word heading and two lines of text, the page is a grid of equal portrait tiles with thin gaps and no card frame. Every teacher is photographed head and shoulders, facing the camera, in the same warm light on the same brown backdrop. Because the portraits match, the grid needs no borders, badges or shadows to look finished.
references.apply: The standard to aim for, and the reason for a photo guide at the publish step: head and shoulders, plain light background, daylight, the face in the upper middle. Eleva cannot photograph every expert, so it fixes what it controls: one crop ratio, the face position and a soft cream backdrop behind small or cut-out photos. Mindfulness and movement studio.
references.query: healthcare provider directory page with portrait cards

references.pattern: A card footer of three labelled cells
references.why: Each card opens with a small round photo, the name, a level tag and the languages, then a bold role line, two lines of text and a row of skill chips that ends in "+13". The footer is three cells divided by thin rules, each a small grey label above a bold value ("171 reviews 4.8", "Orders 133", "Services from $80"). The same fact sits in the same place on every card, so three people can be compared at a glance. The count and the filters sit in one row above the grid.
references.apply: End every Eleva card with fixed cells: "Next time: Thu 26 Nov", "Meets by: Video, in person", "From: €45, 45 min". Put languages directly under the name and cap focus chips at two plus a count. Leave out the work samples and the rating cell. Freelance marketplace; kept for the card structure.
references.query: Zocdoc doctor search results page

references.pattern: Filter chips with icons that open a small panel, and a count beside "Clear all"
references.why: One row holds the search field and six filter chips, each with an icon. A chip that has a value is tinted and says what was chosen ("Design", "Figma & 3 others"), so there is no second row of applied filters. The open chip shows a small panel with a field, a few common choices as buttons, "Clear all" and "Apply". Under the row the result is stated plainly ("3 people found") next to "Clear all", and a list of only a few wide cards still fills the page.
references.apply: Eleva's desktop filters: area, language, how you meet, city, price and free first chat as chips with icons. A chosen chip is tinted and carries its value, and each panel offers the common choices first. State the count under the row with "Clear all" beside it. Hiring marketplace; kept for the filter row.
references.query: Zocdoc doctor search results page

references.pattern: Search written as a sentence, and a result heading that repeats the choices in words
references.why: The search bar has two labelled parts, "Looking for: Product Designers" and "Available for: Mentoring". Under the chip row the heading restates the query with its count ("290 Product Designers" who "Designed a style guide & more"), so the reader can tell what the list is. The one chip with a value is filled dark and the others are outlined. Each card ends with "Available for" chips. A filter panel is open over part of this capture.
references.apply: A two-part search for Eleva ("Help with: Pelvic health", "Meet by: Video") and a heading that reads the result back ("4 pelvic health experts who meet by video in Portuguese"). The sentence replaces the eyebrow and tells the member why these experts are shown. Professional network; kept for the search and the heading.
references.query: healthcare provider directory page with portrait cards

references.pattern: No match: one plain sentence, what other members choose, and a way in for the unsure
references.why: The message repeats the search term and gives two ways forward in one sentence ("Try another keyword, or see what our members are learning"). Five popular items follow as a plain list, each with a small tag for its type. A ruled footer asks "Not sure where to begin?" with a link to a quiz, and a help link sits at the right. The state has no illustration and no dead end.
references.apply: Eleva's no-results state: say what was searched, list the areas or experts members book most, each with a tag (Area, Expert, Free first chat), and close with "Not sure who to choose?" linking to how Eleva works or a free first chat. Use it together with the removable filter chips in reference 08. Learning product; kept for the structure.
references.query: marketplace search results page with no results found

references.pattern: A list of two on a phone: availability in words, one person not available, and help under the list
references.why: Two chips sit above two cards. Each card has a small round photo, the name, an availability line, the languages and focus tags. The first says "Available on Thursday" with the day in the accent colour. The second says "No availability" in grey and stays in the list, so nothing looks broken. Under the short list a tinted block titled "Help is available" offers support to someone in distress. iOS screen from a European health product.
references.apply: On a phone, state availability on every card in words, including "Opening soon" for an expert who cannot be booked yet, and sort those last. End a short list with a block for the member ("Not sure who to choose?" and, in mental health areas, where to get urgent help), not with the invitation to experts. The layout carries to mobile web.
references.query: wellness app practitioner list screen with next available time

references.pattern: List rows that each carry a question you could bring to this person
references.why: Topic chips and a search field sit above a plain list. Each row has a small square photo, the name with a verified mark, one line on who the person is and, at the right, a single question in a soft grey bubble ("What is minimalist entrepreneurship?"). The question shows what this person can help with in the reader's own terms, which a job title does not.
references.apply: Give each Eleva card one line in the member's words under the profession, written by the expert and capped at one line: "Ask me about: pain after birth, returning to running". It helps a member recognise her need on the card. The row layout is also a dense option for a long list on desktop. From an expert question-and-answer product; kept for the row content only.
references.query: coaching marketplace browse coaches page with specialty filter

references.pattern: Areas as a grid of line icons with a short rule under each
references.why: Ten categories sit in two rows of five. Each is a line icon in one stroke weight, a short rule and a label, with wide gaps and no boxes or photographs. The whole catalogue can be read in one glance and takes about a third of a screen.
references.apply: An icon version of Eleva's areas of care for the top of the explorer, where photo tiles would push the first expert down: nine areas in one stroke style from the icon set, a count under each label, and "Opening soon" in grey where nobody is listed yet. On a phone it becomes one scrolling row. Freelance marketplace; kept for the layout.
references.query: services marketplace navigation mega menu

judging_criteria: Can a member narrow the list by area of care, language and how she meets without opening a profile, and do areas with nobody yet show as "Opening soon" instead of disappearing? (02-discovery/04, 02-discovery/03)
Does every card state profession, focus, languages, how you meet, price with session length and the next open time? (02-discovery/01, 02-discovery/02, 02-discovery/09)
Does a card with no portrait still look finished, with no large empty panel? (02-discovery/06)
Is checked registration visible on each card and explained in one sentence above the grid? (02-discovery/05, 02-discovery/07)
Is the current order stated next to the result count, and is paid placement labelled on the card on phones as well as desktop? (02-discovery/11, 02-discovery/07)
When filters leave one or zero experts, can the member remove a single filter from the results area and see what else is close? (02-discovery/08, 02-discovery/10)
On a phone, do filters open in one sheet with a sticky button that shows how many experts will match? (02-discovery/07, 02-discovery/03)
Do the next open time, how you meet and the price sit in the same place on every card, each with a label, and does no value wrap onto a second line at 390px? (02-discovery/14, 02-discovery/02)
Do the portraits in the grid share one crop ratio and face position, so no card looks heavier than its neighbour? (02-discovery/13)
On a phone, do the filter chips and the first expert both show on the first screen, and does a list of one or two end with help for the member? (02-discovery/18, 02-discovery/15)
